title_vi: Tải tệp lớn lên S3: chia phần, chọn cỡ phần, dọn phần bỏ dở

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Các trường hợp dùng kho đối tượng, nơi tệp lớn được tải lên.
Lưu trữ đối tượng so với lưu trữ khối và tệp.

claims.evidence: The Amazon S3 User Guide pages on multipart upload, its limits, object integrity and aborting incomplete uploads were read at the last commit of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide that still held the content (2023); the S3 API model in boto/botocore at a 2026 commit was read for EntityTooSmall and the charging note. The ETag computation was run locally on 2026-10-18 following the documented algorithm; S3 itself was not called.

claims.claim_vi: Multipart upload is three steps (initiate and get an upload ID, upload parts with part numbers 1 to 10,000 and keep each ETag, complete with the list of part numbers and ETags); parts can go in any order, a re-uploaded part number overwrites the earlier part, and on completion S3 concatenates parts in ascending part-number order and the parts no longer exist. The guide advises keeping your own list rather than using the list-parts result to complete.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a, the parent of the 2023 commit that deleted the content.

claims.claim_vi: Part numbers need not be consecutive, except with additional checksums: then the part numbers must be consecutive, and completing with non-consecutive numbers returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.
claims.section: Multipart upload process; Checksums with multipart upload operations
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a after a review finding on PR #144.

claims.claim_vi: An initiated multipart upload does not expire; S3 stores and charges for uploaded parts until the upload is completed or stopped, and recommends a lifecycle rule with AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload.
claims.section: Multipart upload and pricing; lifecycle configuration
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a.

claims.claim_vi: Limits in the 2023 guide: part size 5 MiB to 5 GiB with no minimum for the last part, at most 10,000 parts per upload.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a.

claims.claim_vi: CompleteMultipartUpload fails with EntityTooSmall when a part other than the last is too small; the API reference states the minimum as 5 MB while the 2023 guide's limits table states 5 MiB (5,242,880 bytes), so the lesson tells readers to use 5 MiB; one must complete or abort to stop being charged for parts.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of boto/botocore at commit 4de93abe62cc263980414f7a66be5226bd541b77.

claims.claim_vi: The ETag of a multipart object is not an MD5 digest of the object regardless of encryption. For general purpose buckets with plaintext or SSE-S3 objects, the 2023 guide describes it as the MD5 of the concatenated part MD5 digests followed by a dash and the number of parts; directory buckets and SSE-C or SSE-KMS objects are covered by the separate claims below.
claims.section: Using Content-MD5 and the ETag; multipart uploads
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a.

claims.claim_vi: For directory buckets, the ETag of an object isn't the MD5 digest of the object and MD5 is not supported; the documented MD5-of-part-MD5s recipe applies to general purpose buckets.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of boto/botocore at commit 4de93abe62cc263980414f7a66be5226bd541b77 after a review finding on PR #144.

claims.claim_vi: Computed locally for a seeded random 21 MiB file in 5 MiB parts (5,5,5,5,1): object ETag 4f79d0f27854976ba9c74084e2ea3aee-5 versus whole-file MD5 9cd7fe8ee2fb0c02de53bc4f59b9c0e4; 100 GiB in 5 MiB parts is 20,480 parts, so parts must be at least 10.24 MiB to stay within 10,000.
claims.verified_by: The author ran this Python computation on 2026-10-18 (hashlib); arithmetic from the documented limits.

claims.claim_vi: Multipart upload: initiate, get uploadID, split the file (1.6 GB in 8 parts of 200 MB), upload parts and receive ETags, complete with uploadID, part numbers and ETags, and the store reassembles the object.

An object created by PUT, POST or Copy that is plaintext or encrypted with SSE-S3 has an ETag that is the MD5 digest of its data; with SSE-C or SSE-KMS the ETag is not an MD5 digest of the data; a multipart object's ETag is not an MD5 digest regardless of encryption. The guide does not say the multipart MD5-of-part-MD5s recipe holds for SSE-C or SSE-KMS, so the lesson limits it to plaintext and SSE-S3 objects.
claims.section: Using Content-MD5 and the ETag to verify uploaded objects
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of awsdocs/amazon-s3-userguide at commit cc53dd6a44d3aa1d654e6d3705a0a7550f20fd2a.

design_notes_vi: Một sơ đồ trình tự hai bên cho ba bước, một khung tính cỡ phần từ giới hạn 10.000 phần, một khung hai điều hay quên. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source says a part's ETag is essentially the part's MD5; the lesson follows the S3 guide: whether an ETag is an MD5 depends on encryption, and a multipart object's ETag is never the MD5 of the data.
The lesson adds the 10,000-part limit as the constraint that sets part size, and the cost of incomplete uploads with the lifecycle rule that cleans them up.
The ETag recipe is scoped to general purpose buckets; directory buckets do not use MD5 ETags (botocore API model).
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
